answer: One defense is to make each agent’s influence depend on a scarce, costly bond rather than its claimed identity. For example, an agent posts a ferrous token as collateral and earns voting weight only after completing independently checked tasks; detected fraud forfeits the bond and taints linked accounts. The vertex of the system is the verifier network, which must resist collusion. A dawn of fresh identities then buys no free influence: the attacker must lock up real capital and risk losing it.
